problem_text:
A manufacturing plant is tasked with fabricating four distinct chemical compounds, each of which must undergo four sequential purification stages to be finalized.  
The market value per liter of each compound is detailed below:  
* Compound Alpha yields a revenue of 15.758 per liter  
* Compound Beta yields a revenue of 15.103 per liter  
* Compound Gamma yields a revenue of 7.271 per liter  
* Compound Delta yields a revenue of 19.801 per liter  

The purification time expended per liter for every stage is as follows:  
* For Compound Alpha, Stage 1 consumes 0.94 (liter-hours), Stage 2 consumes 1.301 (liter-hours), Stage 3 consumes 0.896 (liter-hours), Stage 4 consumes 0.285 (liter-hours)  
* For Compound Beta, Stage 1 consumes 1.048 (liter-hours), Stage 2 consumes 0.472 (liter-hours), Stage 3 consumes 0.258 (liter-hours), Stage 4 consumes 1.311 (liter-hours)  
* For Compound Gamma, Stage 1 consumes 1.334 (liter-hours), Stage 2 consumes 0.39 (liter-hours), Stage 3 consumes 1.188 (liter-hours), Stage 4 consumes 0.824 (liter-hours)  
* For Compound Delta, Stage 1 consumes 0.89 (liter-hours), Stage 2 consumes 1.598 (liter-hours), Stage 3 consumes 1.083 (liter-hours), Stage 4 consumes 1.786 (liter-hours)  

The cumulative operational duration for each purification stage is constrained by the available equipment time:  
* The total processing time for Stage 1 cannot surpass 202.109 hours  
* The total processing time for Stage 2 cannot surpass 146.921 hours  
* The total processing time for Stage 3 cannot surpass 141.199 hours  
* The total processing time for Stage 4 cannot surpass 141.016 hours  

Provided that the total duration for each individual stage—Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, and Stage 4—must remain within its respective time limit, determine the optimal production quantities for each compound to maximize overall revenue.
